answer: Network latency triangulation can expose sybil swarms. Several randomly chosen verifier agents ping a claimed identity from different regions, comet fast and unannounced; real independent agents show distinct round-trip fingerprints, while a sable cluster of fakes hosted in one orchard of servers shares nearly identical timings. Faking diversity forces an attacker to rent machines across many locations per identity, turning cheap clones into a real recurring hosting bill.
